name: CLIPBlood
description: White blood cell (WBC) classification from peripheral blood smear images is essential for diagnosing infections, immune disorders, and hematological malignancies.Vision-language models based on Contrastive Language-Image Pretraining (CLIP) offer a promising approach by enabling inference with minimal or no labelled data, yet no prior study has jointly examined models across multiple pretraining domains, prompt strategies, and supervision levels for white blood cell classification.In this work, we present CLIPBlood, a comprehensive benchmark of six CLIP-based encoders for WBC classification on the WBCAtt dataset comprising 10,298 images across five leukocyte classes.The evaluated models span three pretraining domains: general (OpenCLIP ViT-B/32, ViT-L/14), biomedical (BiomedCLIP, PubMedCLIP), and pathology (PLIP, QuiltNet).We assess all models under two complementary settings: zero-shot classification with five prompt templates of increasing domain specificity, and few-shot linear probing with k ∈ {1, 5, 10, 25, 50, 100} labelled samples per class.Our results show that zero-shot performance remains poor across all 30 model-prompt combinations, with no configuration exceeding 0.26 macro-F1, indicating that current CLIP encoders lack the text-image alignment necessary for finegrained blood cell classification.In contrast, few-shot linear probing dramatically improves performance, confirming that frozen CLIP encoders capture discriminative visual structure that can be leveraged w…
